title: Closedness of the local isomorphism locus for two invertible modules on a triple product
statement: Let K be a field [def-weil-field], X,Y,Z schemes over K [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and X,Y proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], with rational points x,y [def-pc-rational-point]. Let M,N be invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] on X×Y×Z [def-pc-fibre-product], whose pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] to {x}×Y×Z and X×{y}×Z are isomorphic. Then the set of t∈Z for which M and N are isomorphic over X×Y×U for some open neighbourhood U of t is closed in Z.

source.place: Tags 0BF0, 0BF3 and 0BF4; source-library theorem of the cube interface

proof.text: Put L=M⊗N∨ and p:X×Y×Z→Z. For every morphism a, an isomorphism a*M≅a*N is equivalent to a*L≅O. The forward implication tensors with the dual; the reverse uses the pullback tensor comparison, evaluation N⊗N∨≅O, symmetry, and associativity to cancel N∨. Thus the two slice isomorphisms give trivial restrictions of L.

The product X×Y is proper and geometrically integral. For geometric integrality, base change to an arbitrary extension field; the base-changed X is integral and locally noetherian, and the projection from its product with Y is geometrically integral by base change of Y. Thus its total space is integral. Consequently p is proper, flat, locally of finite presentation, and geometrically integral. The pair (x,y) gives a section of p. Apply the closed-fibre-locus lemma to L.

The local isomorphism locus equals the fibre-triviality locus of L. One inclusion follows by restricting an open trivialization to the fibre: the canonical fibre map factors through the inverse-image open containing it. For the other inclusion use the arbitrary-fibre openness lemma with the two trivial slice restrictions, and cancel N∨ to recover M≅N over the resulting open.
Rewrite the local-isomorphism set by this equality and use closedness of the fibre-triviality set.
